method: Independent qualitative assessment of documented support, not Gartner research or observed business performance. Ordinal bands are not equal intervals or an aggregate maturity score.

rows.name: Spec Kit — upstream core
rows.scope: Default feature workflow; optional Assess excluded from this row
rows.strength: Technology-independent success criteria and a repeatable convergence loop preserve specification intent through implementation.
rows.boundary: Convergence compares software with spec, plan and tasks; a converged result proceeds to review/PR. Its inventory explicitly excludes post-launch business outcomes.
rows.gap: No required owner receives responsibility for adoption evidence or a post-launch product decision.
rows.impact: Correct software can close the investment before anyone checks whether users gained the intended benefit.
rows.repair: Link the spec to a named adoption owner and a dated outcome decision, using one observable user signal and a guardrail.
rows.proof: A completed pilot review records evidence and an expand, revise or stop decision, linked back to the spec.
rows.indicator_read: The spec template offers user-capability measures such as completion time and task success, alongside quality or later-result examples. These can be useful leading signals, but the core path does not require their cohort, collection window and investment response.
rows.table_gap: No owned outcome review; correct but low-value work can close

rows.name: Spec Kit + Assess
rows.scope: Optional Assess installed and selected before core SDD
rows.strength: Intake, research, definition, shaping and a human-reviewed go/clarify/kill decision can reduce investment in weak ideas.
rows.boundary: An approved assessment hands off manually to specification. Assess is a separate workflow without lifecycle hooks.
rows.gap: The front-end investment decision has no matching outcome review after delivery.
rows.impact: Better initial selection does not tell the sponsor when a once-plausible bet has stopped paying off.
rows.repair: Carry the decision hypothesis and success signal from Assess into a release review with an accountable human.
rows.proof: The first post-release decision explicitly revisits the original evidence and assumptions.
rows.indicator_read: Assess Define asks for success metrics and a current or unknown baseline. This improves the starting question; the post-delivery collection owner, review timing and response remain unconnected.

rows.name: Spec Kit — Yuval PDLC fork
rows.strength: Conviction and value/usability/feasibility/viability assumptions change the execution strategy. Validation consumes real-world evidence and can recommend a pivot or stop.
rows.boundary: A separate validation command can reopen specification; it is not an owned, automatically reached post-delivery review.
rows.gap: Adoption ownership, review timing and decision-ready indicator contracts remain unspecified.
rows.impact: Teams can select a learning strategy yet finish delivery without settling the assumption that justified the work.
rows.repair: Assign one product owner to carry the riskiest assumption through a bounded pilot, threshold-based review and recorded human decision.
rows.proof: One complete spec-to-pilot-to-decision trace changes scope, investment or confidence on the basis of evidence.
rows.indicator_read: Learning telemetry is tied to leap-of-faith assumptions, which is the right intent. The templates do not complete the population, baseline plan, evidence threshold and accountable response contract.

rows.name: Kiro Specs
rows.scope: Documented IDE feature-spec workflow, correctness and hooks; not every Kiro product capability
rows.strength: Requirements, design and implementation tasks provide a clear engineering sequence. IDE correctness properties add systematic checks of specified behavior.
rows.boundary: Task execution and correctness checks establish implementation conformance. User-configurable hooks extend automation but do not supply a product review contract.
rows.gap: The inspected Specs path does not carry product hypotheses, leading signals and an adoption/review owner beyond task completion.
rows.impact: Excellent behavioral checks can validate the chosen solution without establishing that it solves a valuable problem.
rows.repair: Add a linked intent and learning brief, then name the recipient and trigger for the post-launch outcome review.
rows.proof: A spec links a customer assumption to a pilot signal and a documented continue/change decision.
rows.confidence: Medium; official documentation, no configured installation or runtime audit
rows.indicator_read: Acceptance criteria and correctness properties describe behavior to verify. The inspected Specs documents do not require an early customer-value signal, its observation window or a product decision based on it.
rows.table_gap: Conformance can stand in for product value

rows.name: OpenSpec
rows.scope: Default spec-driven schema; explore/propose/apply/archive, with optional verification
rows.strength: Proposals, behavioral scenarios and change archives keep implementation and a durable specification aligned. Optional verification checks completeness, correctness and coherence.
rows.boundary: Apply completes tasks; archive incorporates the change into long-lived specs. Verification is an additional workflow, and warnings do not necessarily block archiving.
rows.gap: The default artifacts explain why a change is wanted but do not require a product measurement or outcome decision after archive.
rows.impact: A coherent history of delivered changes can accumulate without showing which changes improved user outcomes.
rows.repair: Extend the change proposal with one outcome hypothesis and a linked post-adoption review; retain archive as the engineering record.
rows.proof: An archived change points to evidence that led to scaling, revising or retiring the change.
rows.indicator_read: Behavioral scenarios make software conformance observable. They do not by themselves define an adoption or value signal; the default proposal/spec artifacts have no required product-metric response contract.
rows.table_gap: Archive does not establish user benefit

rows.name: BMAD Method
rows.scope: Selected product-brief/PRD/spec/build/retrospective path; not a claim about every quick task
rows.strength: Product briefs and PRDs connect user pain, business success, assumptions and measurable success. The PRD adds countermetrics and risk-sensitive rollout/operations topics; course correction supports human-approved replanning.
rows.boundary: Epic retrospectives inspect integrated behavior and delivery evidence, feeding corrective tickets and a next-epic decision. They do not by themselves require customer-value evidence after launch.
rows.gap: Measurement and rollout prompts are not consistently connected to a named owner, review window and product investment response.
rows.impact: A substantial planning and retrospective process can still judge success using delivery evidence while customer adoption remains unresolved.
rows.repair: Carry one PRD success metric and countermetric into an owned adoption pilot, then bring its result into the next investment decision.
rows.proof: An outcome review changes the next epic or the investment based on customer evidence, not just build quality.

sources.label: PRD success metrics and risk adaptations

rows.indicator_read: The PRD asks for primary and secondary success metrics, definitions, targets and countermetrics, with measurement detail scaled to stakes. It does not consistently connect them to an early learning window and an owner authorized to change the investment.
rows.table_gap: Customer evidence may not affect next investment

rows.name: Compound Engineering — coding path
rows.scope: Brainstorm/plan/work/review/compound; Strategy and Product Pulse not assumed configured
rows.strength: A unified plan separates outcomes from implementation means, preserves requirements and verification, and carries review findings through fixes and explicit shipping checks.
rows.boundary: The inspected shipping contract ends with reviewed work and commit/PR. Operational considerations may enter the plan when material; engineering learning is captured separately.
rows.gap: An outcome-shaped objective does not automatically connect shipped work to adoption evidence and a product decision.
rows.impact: Teams can improve how they deliver each change while learning too little about which changes deserve continued investment.
rows.repair: Add an explicit product handoff to the plan; connect a configured Product Pulse to an owner who must respond.
rows.proof: A shipped plan links to a signal review and a recorded change to product direction or scope.

sources.label: Unified plan: objective, product and verification contracts

rows.indicator_read: The plan distinguishes a user-checkable outcome from implementation means and can add success criteria. Engineering verification demonstrates conformance; no required timely product-signal collection and response follows shipping.
rows.table_strength: Outcome intent, review and corrective delivery
rows.table_gap: Engineering learning can miss product learning

rows.name: Compound + Strategy / Product Pulse
rows.scope: Optional strategy and analytics skills explicitly selected and configured alongside coding
rows.strength: Strategy supplies purpose, users, boundaries and metric sources. Product Pulse distinguishes engagement from value realization, queries real signals and can be scheduled when requested.
rows.boundary: The pulse produces a short report and follow-up questions. A metric report does not itself assign a threshold-based investment decision or adoption responsibility.
rows.gap: The evidence collection path is usable; the accountable interpretation and act-on-results path is incomplete.
rows.impact: More timely evidence may become another report unless someone is responsible for changing the bet when results disappoint.
rows.repair: Name a product decision owner, review cadence and response rules for the primary value signal, including inconclusive evidence.
rows.proof: Two consecutive pulses lead to explicit continue, investigate, revise or stop decisions with follow-through.
rows.indicator_read: The Pulse interview distinguishes engagement from value realization and asks what would be actionable if a signal moves. Its configured queries and time window are substantial strengths. Baselines, response thresholds and an accountable product decision still need an explicit contract.
rows.table_gap: Reports lack an accountable decision response

Upstream: 0: No product framing in inspected scope
2: Repeatable outcome/option exploration; incomplete investment evidence
3: Structured discovery shapes a go/no-go or learning/delivery choice
4: Discovery, evidence thresholds and owned investment decisions form a complete linked contract
Downstream: 1: Rollout/operations prompts or an ad hoc product-validation route
2: A concrete product-signal collection and review/reporting process
3: Adoption ownership plus triggered outcome decisions and routed follow-through
4: Recurring outcome decisions close the loop into subsequent investment and ongoing operation
SDLC: 2: Linked requirements, implementation and basic checks
3: Structured execution plus acceptance/verification and change handling
4: Explicit corrective review/convergence loop with completion criteria
PDLC: 1: Intent framing; delivery remains the completion boundary
2: Substantial discovery or product-evidence mechanisms; lifecycle links incomplete
3: Intent → signal → adoption owner → human outcome decision → next action is required
4: The complete contract recurs across investment, delivery and operation with learning routed forward
